the importance of the methylation of CDKN2A and CDKN2B genes as a marker of disease progression in MDS patients and as an important event during leukemic transformation.
the role of methylation of 9p21 in the pathogenesis of MDS and AML.

hypermethylation of CDKN2A and CDKN2B genes is a frequent event in MDS and AML and is associated with the disease course and prognosis.

methylation changes in CDKN2 genes are associated with disease progression and might be used to monitor the course of the MDS.
